name: Southern Mexico Basin chinampa fields
description: Farmers made productive raised plots in a lake landscape with a network of water channels.

impact.note: Lake-bed raised fields fed the Basin of Mexico's cities, a new way of farming for one region with few known successors elsewhere.

date.label: Approximately 1300–1500 CE
date.basis: Source date for the documented context; BP conversion uses 1950 as reference where applicable.

events.statement: Farmers made productive raised plots in a lake landscape with a network of water channels.

evidence.locator: Un poco de historia and construction
evidence.supports: The author describes artificial cultivated plots and canals in southern Mexico Basin and dates major system expansion approximately 1300–1500 CE. Suggested dates of initial construction differ. Area estimates are model-dependent.

Armillas’s reconstruction estimates more than 120 square kilometres of reclaimed swamp, excluding islands, and more than 9,000 hectares of productive soil after subtracting one quarter for canals and pools. It is a reconstruction using aerial evidence, not a measurement of annual cultivated area. He interprets the regular pattern as evidence for higher-level planning, while the timing of the plan remains uncertain.

events.caveats: The source dates an expansion of the wider southern basin system; the start date of chinampa construction is disputed and this is not a claim of origin.
